help.a.ab_loop: Tap the A-B button to open the section list. Click 'Verse 1', 'Chorus 1', etc. to loop that section. You can pick multiple adjacent sections to loop a wider range. 'Manual' mode lets you tap A while playing to set the start, then B for the end.
help.a.anon_vs_login: No. Anonymous users can analyse, play, calibrate chords and split bars freely. Sign in (Google / Discord) only if you want favorites, ratings, or to file bug reports — features that need an account to attach to.
help.a.audio_kept: At most 10 minutes. As soon as AI analysis finishes the audio is deleted — no copies, no third-party sharing, no participation in other users' search results.
help.a.bar_split: Slices long chords (chords spanning multiple bars) into one-bar cards so they're easier to practise. Pick from 'Split by bar', 'Snap to bar lines' (which nudges boundaries slightly to align), or 'Split by ratio' for proportional cuts.
help.a.beat_upgrade: The default ingest uses a fast librosa beat tracker — great on steady-tempo tracks. For live versions, tempo drift, or older recordings, the madmom tracker (about 30 seconds in the background) is more accurate and re-aligns the chord boundaries to the new beats.
help.a.copyright: You're responsible for ensuring uploads comply with your local copyright law. LiveChord doesn't keep audio copies — files are deleted as soon as analysis finishes — only the resulting chord chart, key, and beat timeline are stored. Please use the service for personal practice only.
help.a.delete_data: Email hiteacherwu@gmail.com from the address you signed in with, mention the service name, and your data will be removed within 7 business days. Data from anonymous analysis is auto-purged within 24 hours.
help.a.fingering: Piano left-hand fingering is generated from the chord root + voicing (5-3-1 / 5-3-2-1 / 5-4-3-2-1 templates). Right-hand melody fingering is intentionally not shown — automatic inference is not reliable enough yet. Guitar / ukulele diagrams use ①②③④ for index / middle / ring / pinky.
help.a.fix_chord: Click any chord card to open a small menu — rename (e.g. C → Cmaj7), delete, merge with the previous or next chord. Or open the full editor from the toolbar's 'Edit' button. After editing, hit 'Save corrections' in the toolbar so the change persists.
help.a.formats: MP3, FLAC, WAV, M4A and OGG. The maximum file size is 200 MB. Embedded cover art is extracted automatically when present.
help.a.how_analyze: From the home page, paste a YouTube URL into the search bar, or click '+ Pick local audio' to upload a file (up to 200 MB; MP3 / FLAC / WAV / M4A / OGG). Analysis usually takes 30 seconds to 2 minutes depending on song length.
help.a.instruments: LiveChord ships five instrument views — each renders the same chord progression from a different angle. Piano shows chord tones + left/right-hand fingering with separate accompaniment and melody rows. Guitar and ukulele show vertical fretboard diagrams plus a right-hand strum / arpeggio pattern. Accordion shows left-hand bass / chord buttons with the right-hand keyboard. Arranger mode bundles backing patterns and chord captions together — close to a Yamaha / Casio arranger workflow.
help.a.ios_install: Open the home page in Safari → tap the Share button at the bottom → 'Add to Home Screen' → 'Add'. Launching from the home-screen icon will open in standalone fullscreen mode.
help.a.login_providers: Google and Discord (Apple is being added). We don't store any passwords; after the third-party verification we keep only your email and display name.
help.a.mobile_play: Mobile browsers block audio until the user interacts with the page (autoplay policy). Tap any chord card or the big play button. If you're using the LINE / Facebook in-app browser some features won't work — open in Chrome / Safari instead.
help.a.report_bug: After signing in, tap '🐞 Report a problem' in the player's bottom toolbar, or email hiteacherwu@gmail.com directly. Please include the song link and the specific behaviour you saw.
help.a.share_third: We do not share personal data. Aggregated, anonymous statistics (total analyses, popular chord progressions) may be cited from time to time, but never with individual-user identifying information.
help.a.speed: Tap the Speed button to cycle through 0.5× / 0.75× / 1× / 1.25× / 1.5× / 2×. 0.5×–0.75× is best for slow practice; 1.25×–1.5× for quick review.
help.a.switch_instrument: Tap the Instrument button in the bottom toolbar (Piano / Guitar / Ukulele / Accordion / Arranger — five icons). Switching is instant — no reload, the chord progression and timeline stay put; only the rendering above swaps. Each browser tab remembers the last instrument you used.
help.a.transpose: Tap the Transpose button (up/down arrows) in the bottom toolbar. Use +/- to shift by semitones, or pick any key from the list. Chord names update instantly. In YouTube embed mode the audio pitch does not change — only the displayed chords.
help.a.upload_vs_yt: If audio quality is the same, a YouTube URL is more convenient (nothing to upload). Upload local files for non-public audio or your own recordings. For live versions or amateur covers, run 'Dynamic beat detection' afterwards so rubato tempo changes are tracked properly.
help.a.what_is_lc: LiveChord turns any audio file or YouTube video into a playable chord chart. AI models detect the chord progression, beats and key, then render the result as an interactive piano / guitar / ukulele view you can practise with.
help.a.what_login_unlocks: Favorites (⭐), recently played, chord-quality ratings, and bug reports. Anonymous users keep full access to analysis, playback, calibration, splitting, transpose, speed, and looping — every practice feature is unrestricted.
help.a.what_we_store: Stored: analysis results (chord timeline, key, beats), upload-file fingerprints, the email and display name from your sign-in provider, and your favorites / ratings / bug reports. Not stored: original audio (deleted within 10 minutes), passwords, payment info, browsing history.
help.a.which_instrument: Depends what you want to practise: practising piano or want to see chord tones clearly → Piano; practising sing-and-strum or memorising chord shapes → Guitar or Ukulele; learning accordion left-hand patterns → Accordion; want arranger-keyboard backing styles (Bossa, Walking, Swing, etc.) → Arranger. You can flip between instruments while the song plays, comparing how each one phrases the same chord change.
help.a.why_wrong: Chord detection runs through an AI model with roughly 80–90% accuracy. It works best on mainstream pop / rock / folk; jazz, dense alterations, live improvisation, synth tones and thin mixes are more error-prone. Use the toolbar's 'Calibrate' and 'Auto-split' tools to fix it, then save the corrected version.
help.a.yt_drm: Some official MVs lock yt-dlp access and analysis fails. Try a cover, live version, or official 'visualizer' upload of the same song; or download the audio yourself and use the upload flow.
help.a.yt_iframe: Some creators block third-party embedding for their videos. LiveChord detects this and offers 'Pick local audio' as a fallback.

sponsor.cta.pending: Tipping setup is in progress. If you'd like to support the project, please email hiteacherwu@gmail.com and I'll reply with the currently available donation methods.
sponsor.faq.a_refund: Buy Me a Coffee treats donations as one-off gifts, so refunds aren't enabled by default. If there's a serious misunderstanding, email hiteacherwu@gmail.com within 7 days and I'll handle it manually.
sponsor.faq.a_tax: Not currently — this is an individual project, so no formal invoice or tax receipt. Buy Me a Coffee sends an email confirmation that can serve as a personal donation record. For corporate sponsorship, partnerships or commercial licensing, please email me.
sponsor.faq.a_why: Exactly — staying free is the LiveChord promise. This page is for users who want to say thanks or who want to help keep the project alive. The cost of a coffee is enough to run the GPU for two extra days, which adds up.

sponsor.hero.title: Support LiveChord
sponsor.intro.body: LiveChord is built, run, and debugged by one person on a single GPU server. Every chord detection tweak, every bar alignment, every piano-fingering visual is the result of countless evenings of tuning and rewriting. It's free to use and always will be.
sponsor.where.body: Total fixed monthly cost is around USD $30, split across three line items:
sponsor.where.gpu: Modal serverless GPU (BTC chord detection) — $3–8/mo, pay-per-use
sponsor.where.r2: Cloudflare R2 object storage (covers, temp uploads) — $1–5/mo, zero egress fee
sponsor.where.surplus: Anything beyond costs goes back into the project: more GPU training time, better beat models, new features (vocal stem separation, more accurate jazz reharmonisation). Every improvement ships as a free update for everyone.
sponsor.where.title: Where the money goes
sponsor.where.vps: CPU VPS (FastAPI, SQLite, beat / accompaniment workers) — $17/mo
